A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RCORE study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original controlled experiments, benchmark evaluations on Sth-com and EK100-com, shortcut diagnostics, and component ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds open-world evaluations and shortcut diagnostics for Jung et al., plus an enhanced RCORE comparison.

M1.justification: Section 5.1 adds RCORE (enhance), applying the framework to C2C (enhance), described as having additional training constraints. This introduces a limited training variant; the primary architecture, CPR synthesis and regularization, and TORC objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Sth-com, EK100-com, and the same controlled and Temporal/Static subsets. The main-text EK100-com counts change from 82 verbs/228 objects to 81/216, matching Table 6 already present in v2; the appendix establishes no corresponding change in dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The comparison substantially expands beyond its previous focus on C2C. Jung et al., previously included only in closed-world Table 3, gains open-world comparisons in Tables 2 and 4. Table 3 adds C2C (enhance) and LogicCAR and removes AIM, which remains in other comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 revises stated FSP/FCP normalization from all unseen samples to misclassified unseen samples, aligning the formulas with Section 3.2. v3 also adds the enhanced-C2C setting for comparison with LogicCAR. Existing splits and Table 7 settings remain unchanged; these revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.2 and Figure 14 examine whether shortcut reliance extends beyond C2C, tracking Jung et al.'s seen/unseen accuracy and FSP/FCP during training. Existing component ablations, failure cases, sensitivity studies, and temporal-shuffling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds Jung et al. results, enhanced closed-world results, and its new diagnostic curve. Under the same documented EK100-com/InternVideo2 setting, Table 4 revises RCORE's seen/unseen/H.M. from 42.32/38.07/40.08 to 41.03/37.31/39.08. Prose also corrects similarity from 0.91 to 0.92 and the EK100 failure-case share from 49% to 39%. Most retained results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 formally introduces the misclassified-unseen index set and corrects FSP/FCP denominators and summation domains. Its FSP error-decomposition formulas also replace membership in frequent compositions with membership in seen compositions. These are targeted mathematical-definition corrections; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: diagnosing object-driven shortcuts, proposing CPR and TORC, and improving unseen compositional recognition on two benchmarks. Added comparisons support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the added Jung et al. experiments as evidence that shortcut reliance occurs across methods and that its benefits are limited under EK100-com's sparse supervision. Existing interpretations of RCORE's mechanisms and applicability boundaries largely remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code repository link. Section 5.1 newly explains the Jung et al. reimplementation and code-availability constraints affecting Jung et al. and LogicCAR. Existing hardware, preprocessing, hyperparameters, and training schedules in Appendix C.2 and Table 7 are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Liu et al.'s Knowledge-driven compositional action recognition and removes Abbasi et al.'s CLIP disentanglement study. It also expands comparative positioning against Jung et al. and LogicCAR while retaining the overall research framing.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the VLM discussion, baseline descriptions, results discussion, and conclusion, plus author-contact and acknowledgement edits. Appendix E gains one subsection and subsequent subsections are renumbered; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the Jung et al. learning-curve Figure 14, expands Tables 2 and 4, and groups Table 3 by standard/enhanced configurations. Existing figures and tables are reflowed or relocated, including the former Figure 14 becoming Figure 15. Figure 7's caption is corrected.

improvement.justification: Expanded baseline comparisons and the cross-method shortcut diagnosis strengthen the existing empirical case. Corrected diagnostic formulas and dataset counts improve consistency, and the code link improves access information. A localized new error limits these gains: v3 calls Jung et al. the lowest-scoring CLIP baseline on unseen Sth-com, although Table 2 reports 25.25 versus AIM's lower 18.50. The added evidence and corrections support a modest net improvement.
